private_notes.observations: In Q1, both firms charged $350; Birchwood Hale received 845 hours and earned approximately $126,696. One quarter does not establish how allocation responds to rate changes.

private_notes.observations: Birchwood Hale held its rate at $350 in both quarters. Raising our rate from $350 to $360 coincided with a decline in allocated hours from 845 to 749 and a decline in quarterly profit.
private_notes.plan: Test a lower rate to see whether the additional hours outweigh the reduced margin. Compare next quarter’s allocation and profit with prior results before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: At $350, allocated hours rose from 845 in Q1 to 915 in Q2 while Arden & Cole raised its rate from $350 to $360. Demand and allocation sensitivity remain uncertain.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q3, we received 1,163 hours and earned $145,373, outperforming Q1 ($350, $126,696) and Q2 ($360, $119,817). Birchwood Hale charged $360 in Q3.
private_notes.plan: Hold the Q3 rate to preserve its strong margin and allocation. Reassess after seeing whether Birchwood Hale changes its rate and how our hours respond.

private_notes.observations: At $360 in Q3, with Arden & Cole at $325, our allocated hours fell to 578 from 915 in Q2. The allocation formula is unknown, but the higher relative rate coincided with a substantial drop in hours and profit.
private_notes.plan: Lower our rate to $330 to improve our relative price while preserving a $130 margin per hour. Assess the resulting hours and profit next quarter before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $325, our hours fell from 1,163 in Q3 to 940 in Q4 as Birchwood Hale cut its rate from $360 to $330. When Birchwood held at $350 in Q1–Q2, our $10 rate increase coincided with 96 fewer hours and lower profit.
private_notes.plan: Set $315 to improve our position against Birchwood's latest $330 rate. The observed sensitivity suggests the additional hours could outweigh the $10 reduction in margin per hour. Reassess against the next rate card and allocation.

private_notes.observations: At $330 against Arden & Cole's $325, we received 850 hours and earned about $110,555 in Q4. Our $360 rate against their $325 in Q3 produced substantially lower profit. The strongest quarters occurred when the competing rate was $350 or higher.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $330 for Q5. This preserves a $130 hourly margin while remaining close to the competitor's most recent rate. Reassess after observing Q5 hours and the new rate card.

private_notes.observations: At Birchwood’s $330 rate, our $315 rate earned about $119,574, slightly more than the $117,483 earned at $325. The higher Q3 profit coincided with Birchwood charging $360.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $315 while Birchwood remains near $330. Reassess if its rate changes or allocation data indicates a different profit-maximizing rate.

private_notes.observations: At $330, allocated hours fell from 850 in Q4 to 770 in Q5 as Arden & Cole lowered its rate from $325 to $315. Q5 profit was about $100,137, below Q4's $110,555.
